discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, beginning with the superfluid-Mott insulator transition

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI Innsbruck, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Feynman proposed using one quantum system to emulate another. Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators (1998) showed that atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model, which made that idea a concrete program. Greiner and Bloch (2002) then observed the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator quantum phase transition, the first clean quantum simulation of a strongly correlated lattice model. Out of this work came a new experimental discipline. It includes the quantum-gas microscopes developed by Greiner and Bloch, with single-site imaging and control, which have revealed antiferromagnetic order and string correlations in Fermi-Hubbard systems. It also includes the observation of many-body localization, and Zoller's theoretical frameworks for analog and digital quantum simulators. Together these advances have settled questions in condensed-matter physics that theory could not settle. They have made ultracold-atom quantum simulators, which are now used in laboratories worldwide, a central platform of quantum science and technology.
